notes: Very cheap and simple. Can be done entirely passively.
Very very low effort, just use Fishing Net and Large Net in Large Island. Make sure to sell these for silver.

Boards are most people's first mastery and GM. Upgrading your sawmill is essential for Sawmill Silver and many masteries. Check out kings page for lots of craftworks ideas for how to use these entirely passively.
A very quick Crystal River mastery.
Can be made entirely from passive production via craftworks. You should definitely GM this early on... probably even MM it.

Another very easy mastery that can be done entirely from passive production. Costs a bit more Board than some others, so this is great for overnight crafting. Ideally you want to turn these into Chum to work on that mastery as well.
When you unlock Glacier Lake you will want to fish there a lot for silver. This will come fairly quickly.

Can be made entirely from passive production via craftworks. You should work on this the same time as you're doing Wooden Barrel, and due to resource saver you should get this first. Don't worry about turning them all into Butter.
Very easy Emerald Beach fishing mastery.
Very easy Emerald Beach fishing mastery.
Once you unlock Pirate's Cove this will be very quick, great silver too.
Quick Lake Tempest mastery.
Should come very quickly once you unlock Glacier Lake.
A very quick fish mastery. It drops in all 4 of the first fishing zones.
You shouldn't really worry about crafting these much, unless you spend a lot of time in Mount Banon. You'll get more than enough to GM from opening Large Chest 01.
Very easy, profitable mastery to work on early. Can be done 100% passive if you want, just make sure to sell when your inventory fills.
Quick Lake Minerva mastery. Make sure you sell as you go.
A quick and painless Glacier Lake mastery. Should be the first or second you get once unlocking the zone.
You don't need to worry about focusing bottles specifically, you will naturally GM them by crafting daily juices and working on Lantern
You will naturally master these while working on other GMs/daily production. Glass.
Quick Glacier Lake mastery.
Fast Pirate's Cove mastery.
Quick Small Island mastery. You can mail these to Geist for friendship xp.
Very cheap, very quick. Turn these into diaries please.

Pretty much the cheapest Mushroom Paste mastery. Do your best to craft these into Essence of Slime or Salt as you go, or the Exchange Center trade for Bell. If you just want to knock out a quick GM though, they're cheap enough to make later that selling shouldn't set you back much.
A quick Stone mastery. Can by done completely passive through Quarry/Craftworks if you want. These sell for decent silver.
The slowest Glacier Lake mastery, but still super fast with how much time you'll spend there for silver.
Very very cheap to craft. Send these to Lorn for friendship xp. Very reasonable MM as well, or a cheap item to manually craft for the Grand Artisan merit badge.
Very cheap, very important for many other crafts. I would definitely recommend putting this in your craftworks after you unlock a few slots.
You should be fishing plenty in Pirate's Cove for silver while you work on leveling and unlocking Glacier Lake and tower levels.
You can make these completely from passive production.
Easy fish from multiple locations.
Byproduct of exploring the forest for nets, and also used in many other masteries. I would recommend that you don't kill your cows as it reduces your Milk production.
Pretty easy and cheap. You get all the materials needed from exploring in Cane Pole Ridge, you'll just need to top up on paste every once in a while.
Quick fishy fish gm.
Quick Pirate Cove mastery. Very easy once you unlock the zone, and great for silver.
You should be exploring forest all the time for Antler. But they also come from plenty of other zones. I would not recommend growing these.

Paste is the base for many other crafts. It will quickly become the root of all your troubles. Luckily you get mushrroms from exploring multiple zones. You will MM paste with multiple GMs that use it still not finished.
Mastery doesn't get easier than this. Can be done passively.
Another Pirate's Cove mastery. Quick and painless.
Very easy GM. You will get progress on this from fishing in Emerald Beach, or just opening Large Chest 01 for Ancient Coin or other gems.
Quick crop that can be grown instantly with Breakfast Boost. Can do these any time, but I'd recommed waiting until they are the CC item, or you can send them to Lorn or Holger
The quickest growing crop. Gm is technically very quick, but requires constant monitoring to be the most effective. Alternatively a few uses of Breakfast Boost will get this done super quick.
Quick gm once you unlock Large Island.
Very quick and easy PC fish.
Slower Minerva fish, but still quick and painless.
You will live and breathe Rope before long.
Opening Large Chest 01 for Borgen shop and the wheel will make this mastery go quickly. Craft into rings if you can afford the paste.
You should be doing plenty of fishing in the Large Island for silver, so this should come very quickly.
Not worth working on until you fully unlock Jundland Desert. It is super fast there.
Another quick and painless Large Island gm.
Another Glacier Lake fish. Should come shortly after unlocking the zone.
After unlocking Glacier Lake, this will come very quickly.
Fishing at Large Island for silver to progress and upgrade production buildings will make this come naturally.
Used to make Glass Orb from Unpolished Shimmer Stone. I don't think you ever need to focus on this mastery, it should just happen over time.
You can craft this, but you will most likely get GM and more just from opening Large Chest 01.
Nice and easy wood, mushroom, and stone craft. Can send to Ric Ryph for some friendship xp, or wait til a valid CC day.
Quick Vast Ocean mastery. Send these to Lorn for friendship xp.
This is one of the easiest fish masteries. You will probably MM this while working on some other VO gms.
The fastest Small Island gm by a longshot.
You should GM this pretty quickly after unlocking Pirate's Cove.
Unlike its cousin Spiked Shell, this is a very easy Large Island mastery. GM will come naturally as you fish for xp and silver.
Emerald Beach has lots of masteries, and this is one of the quicker ones.
Once you unlock Steelworks this will start coming pretty quickly. You will need a goof bit for other masteries, like ((Scissor)), Jade Charm, Red Shield, and others.
Another quick GL mastery once you've unlocked the zone.

You should definitely have some progress on these by the time you start caring about masteries. Sawmill Silver. They're still a great way to turn passive production into silver at any point in the game.
Super quick Crystal River mastery. Nothing special about them though.
The fastest Large Island mastery. Doesn't really look like a Sturdy Sword though to me.
The highest drop rate fish in the entire game. It's worth it to sell in Minerva if you can remember.
You can fish for these, or upgrade your trout farm a bit and bask in the glorious free mastery every day at reset.
Very easy mastery, GM, and even MM. You will need to make tons of twine for other masteries and to make rope for nets.
Explore for these. Emberstone is needed for too many crafts to be using it on glass. It doesn't really matter where you explore, just make use of the other materials in that zone and you'll be fine.
Quick and painless. Great way to use daily feathers, and necessary when working on any of the diary gms.
Cheap mastery that can be done passively. If you can, turn these into Butter Churn.
Very cheap and simple. Can be done entirely passively.
You should be making plenty of these to work on other masteries and Sawmill Silver. Gm, and even MM will come naturally while you work on other things.
Cheap mastery that can be done passively. Try to turn these into either Green Shield or Red Shield if you can.
Can be made entirely from passive production. Make sure you either turn it into Green Scarf or Fancy Drum, or send it to Cecil or Gary Bearson V for friendship xp.
Quick, easy fishing mastery/GM. Found in the first 4 fishing zones. You can send these to Jill for some great friendship xp, or Geist.
Quick to gm, or MM, while working on other Highland Hills masteries. Can also get from opening Medium Chest 02, 5 each.

Very easy GM or MM, able to be worked on at any point in the game. It's best to use your axes for Exchange Center trades, or send to Vincent for friendship XP. You can also explore Small Cave and turn these directly into Spoon as well, provided you can keep up Twine production.
Can be done actively via exploring, or passively via Quarry. Either use it for Explosive, Bottle Rocket, or Beatrix friendship XP.
One of the slower Crystal River masteries, but still quite easy... just spam nets.
There are lots of fish to master at Small Island and this is one of the quicker ones. Send these to Captain Thomas or Geist for friendship xp.
Fairly simple, but useless.
Less use than Blue Dye, but slightly cheaper. Turn it into diaries.
Drops from Small Island or Vast Ocean. The rates are pretty low from both, but you should make good progress while GMing the easiesr fish in each zone.
One of the slower Emerald Beach Fish, but not the slowest.
Forest Pond is a great fishing zone for friendship xp, and a few quick fishing GMs. Send these to Holger.
Can be worked on entirely from passive production. Make sure you upgrade your Trout/Bait Farm and Worm Habitat to keep production flowing. These sell for decent silver as well.
Fairly quick Emerald Beach mastery.

You shouldn't bother with this until you have access to Breakfast Boost. But with that buff it should come pretty quickly, just a matter or clicking a lot. Send your extras to Mariya or wait until it is the CC item.

You shouldn't bother with this until you have access to Breakfast Boost. But with that buff it should come pretty quickly. Send your extras to Mariya for friendship xp, or sacrifice them in the Temple of Reward for small rewards.
It takes a lot of Mushroom Paste, but you should always try to craft your gems into rings when you open Large Chest 01.
Low rates, but you can get them from a few zones. Good for cooking or Mummy friendship xp.

You will definitely GM or even MM these at some point. Daily Antler from your Raptor Pen after you unlock Whispering Creek, and exploring the Forest for them is the main way to make silver late game. Remember, you can't have a Large Net without a Fishing Net.
The hardest Lake Minerva fish (besides golden). But still not that bad. You should get a good bit of Treasure Key while GMing this.
Medium speed Vast Ocean fish. Much quicker than octopus or squid.

You should be crafting these as you explore Whispering Creek for Raptor Egg and levels. You really want to craft Garnet Ring if you can, but sometimes the paste need is too high, in which case you can just sell.
A medium speed Lake Tempest/Crystal River fish, and you can suppliment progress a tiny bit with Grab Bag 02 from the Small Cave.

If you take some time in Highland Hills you can work on both green/purple parchments and diaries. You'll just need to get some extra paste and feathers occassionally to keep up, but it's relatively low effort and fairly quick.
Pretty cheap and quick. Do your best to turn these into Green Shield or Green Scarf, or if you have the rest of the resources Green Cloak.
Medium speed Vast Ocean fish. Much quicker than octopus or squid.
Pretty cheap and low effort. If you wait for passive Straw into Twine into Yarn you don't need to explore much.
Pretty cheap and low effort. If you turn passive Board into Wooden Plank into Wooden Shield you don't need to explore much.
Throw some Green Dye on twine and call it a day.
Please do not craft Jade. Unpolished Jade.
Slower fishing mastery, but still very reasonable.
Great for leveling your crafting skill (if you need xp, make sure you manually craft, no craftworks) and for silver.
The easiest diary, and the easiest to get rid of. Send these to Mariya for friendship xp.

Definitely try to craft these with mastery bonuses on, Mushroom Stew and an event bonus if possible. Also do your best to sell these during events, especially with IOTD bonus an Shrimp-a-Plenty. Production is almost entirely trhough pets, so will be very slow.
Quick Board/Glass mastery. Great to work on with glass from Ember Lagoon, or while exploring CPR.
Pretty quick board/glass mastery, also sells for decent silver early on. Great to work on alongside Lemon Quartz Ring in CPR.
Reasonable fish mastery that you can work on from both Vast Ocean and Emerald Beach.
Pretty much just Pearl and some Twine. Easy, and great to work on while opening chests for AC... If you can keep up with the Twine.
Very easy GM or MM, able to be worked on at any point in the game. You can also explore Small Cave and turn these directly into Bone Pickaxe
Looks harder than it is, honestly.
A medium speed Emerald Beach mastery. Also a cool emblem that some notable community members use.
A quicker Emerald Beach mastery. Nothing fancy, just lots of Fishing Net and Large Net.
You can get these in both Vast Ocean and Emerald Beach, so you'll get it pretty quick if you're working on other fishing masteries.
Easy ring mastery. Great to work on during Borgen days.

After unlocking Steelworks, you can produce these passively via Craftworks. Speed will be based on your production, how often you sell, and whether you dedicate time to actively crafting them. Overall pretty cheap to make though.
Slower gm, but relatively easy. Just keep dropping nets in Emerald Beach.
If you've got Mushroom Paste it's super quick and easy while opening Large Chest 01. (Good for borgen days, or spinning the wheel).

Once you unlock Steelworks you will start getting passive progress every hour. Upgrading steelworks is expensive, so if you may need to actively work on these. Turning them into Crossbow is a great profit.

Another fishing mastery that can be worked on in both Emerald Beach and Vast Ocean. It's slower than most in either zone, but working on it from both will get it fairly quickly. Send these to Geist for some friendship xp.
Just needs a lot of wood/boards/planks. You can do this fully from passive production with craftworks.
Using Mushroom Paste and Leather from exploring the forest and passive Steel this goes pretty quick, and costs very little. Can sell or donate to a raptor in rfc.
Full wood mastery, can be done entirely from passive production and craftworks.
Needs lots of Board, but luckily we can make those hourly via sawmill! Another potentially passive mastery thanks to craftworks.
Cheap mastery that can be done passively.

Fairly cheap and easy mastery when you start upgrading production buildings. If you're exploring for the Arrowhead, you iwll probably have to take breaks in order to fill up on twine again, since you should be making Fishing Net as well.
Can be done entirely from passive production.
Can be done entirely from passive production. Mailable for some reason. Send them to LinkJason10j for fun.

Needs paste, but pretty cheap and quick overall. Not much else to do in Small Spring though while collecting Aquamarine, so try to make the most of the Feathers you get while working on this. Can also get from opening Medium Chest 02, 5 each.

You should only really work on this with Grape Juice and Mega Beet Seeds; either from your Strange Onion pet, or the Exchange Center. Make sure to use Mushroom Stew and it will be pretty quick. Sell, don't void, since they're worth a lot.

One of the main reasons to explore Misty Forest. You should turn these into Blue Purse so you can make a lot of silver. If you don't have those unlocked yet, or have already finished, you can knock out ((Fancy Pan Flutes)) pretty wuickly, if you can keep up with the Wood needed.
Work on this while doing Coin Purse and Blue Dye to make some easy silver.
Medium difficulty Small Island fish, just keep throwing nets at the zone.
Throw some Blue Dye on twine and call it a day.
Use passive coal from Quarry to make Black Powder, passive Wood from Sawmill, and either Feathers from daily chickens or from exploring Highland Hills or Small Spring. It should go very quickly.
Swamp

Most people overlook this fish, even though it's pretty easy. That's likely because the other easy Farm Pond fish also come from other locations, and they normally get GMed from those. Send these to Holger or Thomas.

Don't work on this GM until you have access to Breakfast Boost, whether by cooking it yourself, or trading. It's rather painless with the meal, just a bunch of clicking. Send your spares to frank, or Rosalie/Charles Horsington III.
Catfish have a pretty low drop rate from fishing in the Farm Pond. Luckily you can also get them from opening Grab Bag 01, which you get from fishing in the Forest Pond. So don't stress.
Make sure you turn these into Blue Purse as much as possible, because the silver is really good.
The hardest part of this mastery should be the Steel Wire, so make sure your steelworks is upgraded a bit to help out. The upside is that these sell for great silver, which you can reinvest.
Quite cheap and painless. Great use for Hammer so work on this while you work on those. Sells for decent silver too.

The harder of the two Black Powder masteries, as it uses Board instead of Wood, but still pretty cheap overall. Save working on this until you can mail them, and send them to Beatrix for friendship xp.
Definitely a harder fishing mastery. But at the end of day it's still just making and using more large nets.
Try to make these when exploring Whispering Creek for Raptor Egg and xp. They sell quite nicely.
Great to work on if you're exploring Black Rock Canyon for Large Chest 02 or Orange Gecko. If you wait for passive Twine even GM is pretty cheap.
Pretty easy and cheap. I would reccomend crafting these into Purple Bag so you don't have to come back and make more. Also purple ones sell for good silver.
It uses a good amoutn of Leather, but it's relatively simple overall. Great for knocking out a few masteries at a time if you do it along with its components.

You will get this over time from crafting your daily fruits into juices, as well as some quests, potentially the T80 perk, and Wheel of Borgen. I don't think it's necessary to 'actively' work on this.
Starts out pretty slow, but before you know it this will be GMed. EL is a great place to explore and you can work on this via exploring directly, or crafting up Prism Shard.
Large Net Large Net Large Net
A very quick Pirate Cove mastery. You'll be fishing there a lot while leaving up and earning silver for tower, so this will come naturally before you know it.
A slower Vast Ocean mastery, but at the end of the day it boils down to just using a lot of nets, so not very hard.

You will get this over time from crafting your daily fruits into juices, as well as some quests, potentially the T80 perk, and Wheel of Borgen. I don't think it's necessary to 'actively' work on this.

Honestly, more people should have this GMed than actually do. It's a fairly fast crop once you have the T10 perk, and you can get a lot from opening Grab Bag 01 from the forest pond. Sacrifice them at the Temple, or send to Holger for friendship xp.

If you take some time in Highland Hills you can work on both green/purple parchments and diaries. You'll just need to get some extra paste and feathers occassionally to keep up, but it's relatively low effort and fairly quick.
Pretty easy GM. A step on the path to diary GMs while exploring HH.
Pretty simple WC mastery. I would turn them into Red Shield first, then Red Trunk as you work on oak masteries, then back to Red Shield for the silver.
Slightly harder than Red Dye, and less uses. But it's easy.
Pretty cheap. Great to make while working on Hammer mastery, and always turn these into Leather Belt if you can. There's also a decent amount needed for quests.
Good to work on while exploring in Misty Forest. Needs lots of Wood.
Swamp
Swamp
A bit costly to explore for all the Bone you will need, Small Cave holds all of the resources needed.
Slow Vast Ocean GM... But at the end of the day it's still just tossing nets, so low effort.
Requires a good bit of paste, but otherwise cheap.

Definitely try to craft these with mastery bonuses on, Mushroom Stew and an event bonus if possible. Also do your best to sell these during events, especially with IOTD bonus an Shrimp-a-Plenty. Production is almost entirely trhough pets, so will be very slow.
Daily production from Raptor Pen, exploring Forest, and quests are your friend. Large Net are life.
The most annoying ring, because it takes 2 different gems, and 3x Mushroom Paste. Still fairly easy compared to some masteries though.
Slap two pieces of paper together with some mashed mushies and bang, you got a book!
Great for silver!
A bit costly to explore for all the Bone you will need, but if you use passive Twine, the Small Cave holds all of the resources needed.
Swamp
Pretty reasonable mid to late game mastery. Doesn't need crazy resources. Benefits a lot from upgrading sawmill and hayfield.

The biggest drawback is just waiting for it to process. Dump whatever extra crops you might be voiding in, or daily Broccoli from pets is great too. There is a perk to make the mill process twice as fast, if you want to go for MM it's a good investment, otherwise don't bother.

Each wheat makes 14 flour, so you don't need a crazy amount of wheat to GM this. There's a perk that makes the flour mill process twice as fast. Probably don't buy it unless you're rich or want to MM flour.

Grown from Gold Cucumber Seeds, if you have them, or a rare chance from Cucumber Seeds. Also you can get these from Grab Bag 01 which is from fishing at the Forest Pond. This is the easiest gold crop because of this.
Another paste mastery, but it's actually not that bad with Sand from Jundland Desert. I personally would explore Forest for the Mushroom Paste and Wood needed.
Easy JD mastery. Ideally you want to turn these into Spool of Copper, but copper is way harder to get than other JD mats.
Swamp
Medium speed mastery, good for silver. Can make even more if you explore forest for the leather and wait for passive Twine/Rope to come in.
Needs lots of Purple Flower, but it's easy enough. Use it to make Purple Bag and Belt Drive.
Throw some Purple Dye on twine and call it a day.

Great use for Oak from grinding WC, but it needs Mushroom Paste, Twine, AND Steel, which are all individual sticking points when doing a lot of exploring and crafting. Good for crafting xp and selling for silver as well.
Long cook time, which means you get mastery progress quickly from actions. Also good for cooking xp.

You will naturally master this just trying to do quests. There are plenty of uses for corn, between cooking, rfc, and Corn Oil, so if you want to knock it out as a GM, you can fish in Pirate's Cove and open the Large Chest 03 to help out.

Uses both Leather and Mushroom Paste, which are side products of exploring in the Forest, but sadly uses Yarn too, which you cant make at the same time because you'll need the straw for rope to make nets. I suggest working on this either from trading for the paste/leather, or off an on when not actively exploring forest for nets.
Fairly cheap, but slow if you wait for passive Steel Wire from steelworks. If you actively explore for it, you can get it done way quicker, but the cost increases a lot.
Long cook time, which means tasting is really effective. The Red Berries cost is pretty high, so make sure you're working on other WC masteries when you explore so you're not voiding.
Medium level craft. Good way to use up Red Dye from WC after finishing Red Shield, without the heavy Steel cost of Red Trunk.

With Mega Sunflower Seeds and Grape Juice this goes pretty quick, you'll just need to wait for your Onion pet to bring enough seeds. Don't forget to use a Mushroom Stew for great mastery prgress each harvest.
Swamp
Steel and Emberstone are used in lots of crafts now. Luckily this one there are no other components. It's pretty realistic to GM these in a few days if you're actively working on them.

Fairly easy to master, but GM will take some time. You also get a good amount from quests and some from pets over time. If you care about GM, use Mushroom Stew when claiming large amounts from quests.

You will always want to turn your lemonade into AP, but this will probably take a long time to GM. If you care about GM on this, make sure you're using Mushroom Stew for quests that reward more than a few hundred.

You will definitely want to be working on these when exploring Jundland Desert. If possible, use them to make Engine, but those can be quite costly so in my opinion it's fine to sell extras if you can't.
Swamp

This has a shorter cook time, so you won't get as much mastery progress from tasting as longer meals, but it is very cheap to make, so if you're actively working on this mastery it can go rather quickly.

The slowest growing mailable crop. Because of that it's easy to avoid growing these and just buy. They have a decent grow length where you can plant them, do a few things, and come back and reset. Also useful for cooking.
You will need a lot of these for cooking, but it still takes a while to GM them.
Slower mastery to start, but you'll need a bunch for quests and cooking. At some point you may start voiding it if you're using Large Chest 03 to get Corn.
See note for leeks.

Watermelon is the fastest non-tradable crop. If you buckle down and work on GM it will still take a while, but you can stock up on some Piece of Heart in the process. If you're going to void, Feed Mill or Temple are good places to send your extras.

Long enough that you don't want to be growing it all day, but not quite long enough to justify using Grape Juice on it regularly in my opinion, unless you need it for quests. Also brought by 3 pets, which is nice.

See the notes on Broccoli above, but this time it's brought by 4 pets instead. Not that that helps much for mastery. You need more than 40k for quests, which gets a good chunk of the GM out of the way.
It grows pretty quick after you unlock the first Tower artifact, but there's not much to do with it after you've grown it. You can send it to Beatrix, George, or Vincent for some friendship xp.

The cheapest Engine component, if that counts for anything. Easy enough you shouldn't worry too much about crafting these up and selling if you just want to focus GM and not spend your entire life savings and time making engines.
One of the friendlier JD crafts. You'll need lots for all the Corn Oil needed for other masteries.

Slow enough crop that you shouldn't feel bad about using Grape Juice on them. In the past they've been needed a lot for the December event (Crafting Christmas Tree and Holiday Wreath ) and the winter 'season' (Small chance of Frozen Pine when harvesting), so if that time of year is coming up, hold off on GM for then.
Fast enough that using Grape Juice or cookies doesn't make sense, but slow enough that GM will take a few weeks probably.

Only viable way to work on this is daily Grape Juice. Make sure you have Mushroom Stew active, and maybe even some cookies. Sell extras to avoid voiding, or you can use a bit in cooking ( Shrimp-a-Plenty ).
Needs Emberstone and Small Bolt, neither of which is really fun to get. But more reaosnable number than some other things. Plenty of items to craft these up into while working on GM.
Requires just enough Purple Flower and Leather to be annoying. It's really not a hard mastery, just inconvenient.
Pine Tree...

Bone Broth is technically the hardest "Meal" to master/GM because you get almost no mastery progress from tasting. It's also the easiest, because it has been offered at Borgen's a few times, but you are always limited on how much you can buy based on inventory cap. It is not sellable, so you have to use it to cook other recipes to make space.
Relies on daily Milk production, which is limited by inventory and cow levels. Can go quicker if you trade for milk, but will probably still take a very long time.
War is expensive.

The amount of Oak needed for these is insane. They also need a good amount of Mushroom Paste which can get annoying fast. Most people that have GMed these just did it because they were bored, genuinely. Plus side is, you'll get loads of Raptor Egg while working on it.
Lower-cook time meal, which means tasting gives less mastery, but relatively cheap. Gm will take a long time.
Requires a ton of Emberstone. Going for mastery on this is reasonable, but GM is just a flex goal at this point, in my opinion.
The main drawback on with this is the high Corn cost. Mastery is expensive, but you can get it done in a reasonable time. GM is out of the question in my opinion.

Cotton has a long enough growth time that it's no fun at all to grow. Luckily you don't really need it a ton, and 2 pets bring it. You'll probably master it while working on quests, but GM will be a long journey.
You will probably get regular mastery for this naturally while working on quests and other GMs, but GM will require a lot of resources and/or time. Macaw brings these.
TBD
A lot goes into this craft, but the main limiting factor is probably going to be Transistor as you go. Mastery will take a while, GM will take forever.

The hardest part of this is the Cotton. At 6 per chair you will need a significant amount. I would recommend using daily grape juice for the cotton, along with any crop multiplying meals on Mega Cotton Seeds.
Requires both Corn Oil and Steel Vise, as well as tons of Oak. The only upside is the sell price.

Annoying to GM, because it takes Cotton to craft. But with all of the Grape Juice perks and the T150 artifact you can grow quite a bit in a day and get some solid progress. You can also get them via Mystical Chest 02 from fishing in Pirate's Cove.

Pretty slow mastery/GM. You really shouldn't need a lot of tea in your daily play, so selling is probably okay. Make sure you're working on other CPR masteries like Lemon Quartz Ring and something with Glass Orb so you're not wasting resources.
GM will take a long time, but this is one of the cheaper meals to make. It's mostly crops that can be grown instantly with Breakfast Boost.
Like most JD crafts, this will take a while. It's not very complex, it just needs lots of exploring in Jundland for all the Prickly Pear.
Requires Moonstone, which will take a while. Over 60k are needed for quests, which is a lot of mastery.

The biggest hold up is exploring JD for Copper Wire to make Spool of Copper. You can grow the potatoes or fish for them (via Grab Bag 01 ) in the Forest Pond. You'll need 30k of these for the COI questline, so plan accordingly.
Swamp

Honestly this rating is partially just based on the fact that you don't really ever need a large amount of pumpkins for anything. They have a long enough grow time that Grape Juice makes sense to grow them, but it would only be for mastery. Most other crops are needed more for quests or crafting, or season events.
Uses a good bit of resources, but still fairly easy if you wait for passive Steel. Sells for okay silver, but in general Red Shield is better profit for mostly the same materials.
Longer cook time, so you will get more mastery per taste. The biggest draw back is the Honey needed to cook it.
Very slow, but easier than the likes of Sea Dragon or Crab Claw.
There isn't much point to growing a lot of wheat other than Flour and a few quests. If you've already done longer crops it makes sense to use some Grape Juice on it.
Good way to use up Acorn, but it needs so many that GM will take a long long time. Always make sure you're tossing them here instead of voiding though.
Requires Amber, which is a Super Rare, and costly to explore for. You get it from your Lemur at level 6, but not enough to go for GM, or even mastery really.
So far, the seeds for flowers are quite limited. Even using all cookies it requires many seeds to get mastery, and a crazy amount for GM.
Very high resource cost (it's mostly Cabbage, which take forever to grow).

The only way to craft more Compass is to toss them into the Wishing Well, then recraft with the Magna Core you get back. It's very expensive, as each costs 4x Small Screw and your free tosses into the well are limited.

If you don't have a stockpile of Small Screw, this is the single most stam-intensive craft currently in the game. It's quite costly, but you should definitely be crafting these up into Engine as you go.
Requires multiple Corn and Red Twine, so very slow mastery. Quite a few are needed for quests, so you will need to make some, but GM/MM are not super attainable.

The amount of stamina and mental drain to craft these will drive you mad. Many different components, with many different zones necessary. The biggest cost is all of the Small Screw and Small Spring you will end up needing.
One of the most expensive crafts in the game, even moreso than Engine.
Small Screw are quite limited and/or costly, so GM will be a long road. Mastery is still hard, but doable with time. Steelworks also occassionally produces these.
